Targ. O. Gen. XXXVIII, 15 (Y. כעיסת). Ib. XLVII, 18; a. fr.—Part. pass. מְכַסָּא unknown, remote.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on II Kings 19:2">Targ. II Kings XIX, 2</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on II Samuel 13:2">Targ. II Sam. XIII, 2</cite> (h. text <he>ויפלא</he>); a. e.—
<cite ref="Shabbat 156b:6">Sabb. 156ᵇ</cite> <he>כַּסִּי רישיך וכ׳</he> keep thy head covered in order that the fear of the Lord may rest upon thee.
<cite ref="Shabbat 125a:2">Ib. 125ᵃ</cite> <he>לכַסּוּיֵי בהו וכ׳</he> to cover a nuisance with it.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 52">Gen. R. s. 52</cite>, [read as:] <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 91:1">Yalk. ib. 91</cite> <he>וכסי עיניך מינאי</he> and close thine eye from upon me, i.e. take the indulgence money.
<cite ref="Taanit 25a:16">Taan. 25ᵃ</cite> <he>רקיע</he> … <he>כסי פניך ולא אִיכַּסִי</he> ‘cover thy face, O sky,’ but the sky was not covered.
<cite ref="Chullin 87a:1">Ḥull. 87ᵃ</cite> <he>אפשר … ומְכַסֵּי בחדא</he> he may kill with one hand and cover (the blood) with the other; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to be covered, hidden; to cover one’s self; to conceal one’s self, withdraw.
